Edit one document's body — atomic content-anchored partial edits

Edit one document's body with atomic, content-anchored partial edits.

The ops are an ordered array applied all-or-nothing, each against the result of the prior. Any anchor that fails to match refuses the whole batch (exit 2) and writes nothing — a `str_replace` whose `old` is missing, or matches more than once without `--replace-all`; a heading that names two sections, which refuses as ambiguous rather than guessing. Replace a whole body, or change frontmatter, with `norn set` instead.

USAGE
    norn edit [OPTIONS]

ARGUMENTS
    <DOC>
        The doc to edit. Path, stem, or wikilink-shaped (with or without [[]])

OPTIONS
        --edits-json <JSON>
        The edits as a JSON array of ops (e.g. `[{"op":"str_replace","old":"a","new":"b"}]`). Mutually exclusive with stdin; if omitted, the array is read from stdin

        --str-replace <OLD>
        Sugar: `str_replace` — the OLD anchor. Payload: `--new` (alias `--content`)

        --replace-section <HEADING>
        Sugar: `replace_section` — the HEADING anchor. Payload: `--content`

        --append-to-section <HEADING>
        Sugar: `append_to_section` — the HEADING anchor. Payload: `--content`

        --delete-section <HEADING>
        Sugar: `delete_section` — the HEADING anchor. No payload

        --insert-before-heading <HEADING>
        Sugar: `insert_before_heading` — the HEADING anchor. Payload: `--content`

        --insert-after-heading <HEADING>
        Sugar: `insert_after_heading` — the HEADING anchor. Payload: `--content`

        --new <NEW>
        Payload for `--str-replace` (the replacement text; JSON field `new`)

        --content <BODY>
        Payload for the section ops (JSON field `content`); also an alias for `--new` on `--str-replace`

        --replace-all
        Replace all matches for `--str-replace` (JSON field `replace_all`)
        Possible values: true, false

        --expected-hash <HASH>
        Refuse the edit unless the document's current content hash equals HASH (blake3 hex of the full file — the `document_hash` plan ops carry). Opt-in compare-and-swap; absent = read-modify-write

        --yes
        Apply the change without an interactive confirm prompt
        Possible values: true, false

        --dry-run
        Preview the change without writing
        Possible values: true, false

        --format <FORMAT>
        Output format; `json` emits the mutation-report envelope
        Possible values: records, json

GLOBAL OPTIONS
    -C, --cwd <CWD>         Run as if norn started in this directory (default: $NORN_ROOT, else the current directory)
        --verbose           Include full diagnostic detail in output
        --no-cache-refresh  Skip the implicit cache refresh before reading the graph
        --color <COLOR>     Color output. Honors NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE.
        --vault <NAME>      Target the registered vault with this name (see `norn vault register`)

Documentation: https://github.com/dbtlr/norn
